title: Intrinsic and K-flat augmented-tower derived completeness agree
statement: For a prime l, a finite-dimensional extension E of Q_l, a scheme Y, an auxiliary finite-field datum D with l != D.p, and a derived completed-integral coefficient object K, IsSfDerivedComplete l E Y K holds if and only if IsDerivedComplete l E Y D hl K. Both conditions use the canonical coefficient quotient units and transitions; no boundedness or constructibility is assumed. The definitions are those of def-weil-derived-complete and def-weil-integral-reduction-tower.

source.place: Definition 3.5.2; the canonical map to the derived reduction limit, computed on K-flat resolutions; Stacks Tags 06YY and 06YL

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution of a representative of K. The universal derived-change-of-rings counit is invertible on its K-flat source; exact restriction and its localization factorization give the levelwise isomorphism from each intrinsic reduction to the ordinary tensor complex.

The normalized derived tensor/restriction adjunction identifies the localized chain unit with the intrinsic derived unit followed by the representative comparison. Uniqueness of the legacy unit and transition maps on pure tensors identifies them with the intrinsic chain maps. The characterization of sfDerivedReductionTransition on K-flat representatives therefore makes the levelwise comparisons an isomorphism of augmented towers.

Transport the product witness along the levelwise isomorphisms. The product of these maps commutes with 1 minus the shift by transition compatibility, and with the augmented product map by unit compatibility. Construct the isomorphism of Roos triangles explicitly. Distinguishedness is invariant under this isomorphism, giving the desired equivalence for every resolution. Existence of a K-flat resolution gives the forward implication; a resolution witnessing legacy completeness gives the reverse implication.
